The Secret Briefing Circus: When the Prophecy Crowd Mistook a Nothing Burger for the Marriage Supper

There are times when the only sane thing left to do is laugh, not because deception is funny, not because devils are imaginary, not because strong delusion is a joke, and not because the Bible believer is asleep at the wheel, but because the circus has gotten so loud that a little sanctified mockery may be the only medicine left for folks who still have enough Bible sense to smell the elephant tent. We have lived through enough public theater to know how this game works. We had COVID panic, expert panels, emergency language, moral pressure, social shaming, shifting stories, and enough “trust the science” sermons to make a blind man ask who wrote the liturgy. We had Epstein-file teasers that turned into another government fog machine. We had balloons floating across the country like somebody’s birthday party got lost over Montana, and half the internet was ready to declare war on helium. We had drones, UFO hearings, classified-file promises, “very soon” announcements, and now here comes the prophecy crowd with their hair on fire, their microphones polished, and their thumbnails screaming like the Beast just checked into a motel outside Nashville.

And what is the latest act? A group of pastors and charismatic prophecy personalities supposedly get pulled into secret briefings, no phones, no cameras, no recordings, no documents, no open testimony, no way to test it publicly, and we are all supposed to sit up straight like Moses just came down from Sinai with a manila folder marked “UAP Disclosure.” They say the government is worried the Church is not ready. The world system, which has spent decades mocking Genesis, censoring Bible truth, promoting every moral confusion under the sun, and treating Christians like uneducated leftovers from a pre-scientific age, has suddenly developed a tender pastoral burden for the faith of the saints. Please. Since when did Caesar call a prayer breakfast because he was worried Galatians might not survive the news cycle? Since when did Pilate send a memo to the apostles saying, “Brethren, Rome has some troubling interdimensional material, and I fear this may shake your confidence in the resurrection”? If the thing is real, say it. If it is not ready to be said, stop selling tickets to the whisper campaign.

That is the smell of it. The whole thing has the smell of theater. Not because something spiritual will never happen. It will. Not because the devil has no plan. He does. Not because lying wonders are not coming. They are. But the Bible already tells us the order, the character, the purpose, and the end of these things. The Church is not waiting for devils to come down; the Church is waiting to go up. The world may be prepared for a lie, but the body of Christ has been given the truth. The Lord told us the end from the beginning. He did not say, “I have many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now, so wait until a few charismatic preachers get invited to a private Airbnb briefing with no phones.” He said, “If it were not so, I would have told you” (John 14:2). The last prayer of the Bible is not, “Even so, release the files.” It is, “Even so, come, Lord Jesus” (Revelation 22:20). That is the difference between Bible prophecy and prophecy vaudeville.

Chapter 1: The Government Suddenly Cares About Your Bible?

Let us start with the comedy built into the premise. The same system that wants God out of schools, God out of law, God out of public life, God out of creation, God out of marriage, God out of biology, and God out of conscience is now supposedly worried that Christians may not be spiritually prepared for UFO disclosure. That is rich. That is like Pharaoh calling Moses into a private meeting because he is concerned Israel may not have enough devotional material for the wilderness. That is like Nebuchadnezzar hosting a seminar on how to resist image worship. That is like Jezebel
